newsitem.title: NORWAY: Elderly Germans' Arctic cruise ordeal ends.
newsitem.headline: Elderly Germans' Arctic cruise ordeal ends.

text.p: Scores of elderly German holidaymakers headed for dry land on Thursday after an ordeal in which their cruise liner ran aground and they had to be transferred to a rescue ship surrounded by treacherous Arctic ice.
Officials said the Hanseatic, a German-owned cruiser, headed for the settlement of Longyear on the Norwegian Arctic island of Spitzbergen after being refloated from a sandbank early in the morning.
The 9,000 deadweight-ton liner had been stuck fast off northern Spitzbergen since Sunday. Efforts to pull her free had been hampered by drifting ice.
The 145 passengers, mostly German and with an average age of 70, were taken off shortly before the liner was dragged off the sandbank by a Norwegian coastguard ship.
They were later allowed back on board.

Officials said the ship, with a crew of 115, left after an inspection of the hull showed it was not damaged. They said it would arrive early on Friday in Longyear, where the passengers would be put on a charter flight to Hamburg.
Coastguards unloaded the ship's 480 tonnes of heavy fuel oil before dragging her free at 3.45 a.m. (0145 GMT).

The ship's owner, Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG, had originally planned to start evacuating passengers at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT), but the wind changed late on Wednesday and pushed away the icefloes massed around the liner.
